executive_summary: Across 24 paired ablation episodes (4 medium and hard worlds x 3 policies x 2 text providers), injected cognitive-bias workplace chatter alters LLM investigation trajectories without corrupting final accusation accuracy. Both carbon (acc=1.00, 4/4 true moles accused) and the Bayesian solver (acc=1.00) achieve 0.00 decoy and rumor-target false accusation rates under BiasedChatterProvider and TemplateProvider alike, whereas obvious_heuristic collapses to acc=0.00 and score_mean=-1.000 in both arms (50% framed_decoy, 25% overlapping rumor_target, and 50% grudge_persona accusations) without ever querying messages (msg_calls=0). Under biased chatter, carbon reads the Day-1 unverified rumor bc1-0 in 75% of worlds (3/4), increasing rumor_distract_rate from 0.50 to 1.00, quadrupling rumor_action_share from 0.0103 to 0.0431 (+0.0328), and increasing message tool calls from 19 to 35 (+16 calls; msg_budget_share 0.1392 vs 0.0672) via initial empty-query errors and recurring single-vowel searches. Despite this distraction tax, carbon_biased achieves a slightly higher pooled score than carbon_template (+0.662 vs +0.642, score_delta=+0.020; mean_day 9.75 vs 10.75; mean_steps 84.8 vs 105.0) due to strong seed-level divergence: in hard:s0, reading bc1-0 delays canary deployment and triggers 3 rumor-target interviews plus 2 sender interviews, dragging score down by -0.170 (+0.580 on Day 11 vs +0.750 on Day 6 in template); conversely, in medium:s10 (+0.760 vs +0.680), medium:s11 (+0.650 on Day 9 vs +0.600 on Day 14), and hard:s1 (+0.660 on Day 11 vs +0.540 on Day 15), canary version leaks override biased chatter while carbon_template gets bogged down in 79- to 82-interview sweeps (143 to 146 steps). Finally, solver demonstrates near-total chatter invariance (score_mean=+0.715, score_delta=0.000, mean_day=7.25, steps_delta=+0.5, rumor_action_share=0.0000), never reading matched bc messages (msg_reads=0) and isolating moles purely through combinatorial canary splits (mean_canaries=8.25) and access-log intersections.

clusters.title: Rumor-Target and Rumor-Sender Verification Delay
clusters.mechanism: When BiasedChatterProvider injects bc1-0 (unverified_rumour) on Day 1+, carbon surfaces bc1-0 via Day-2 vowel searches and calls read_message(id=bc1-0) in 3 of 4 biased episodes (75% read rate). Reading the rumor diverts action budget toward interviewing the innocent rumor_target (100% rumor_distract_rate vs 50% in template; rumor_action_share rising from 0.0103 to 0.0431) as well as the rumor sender. This failure mode peaks in hard:s0:carbon:biased, where reading bc1-0 (sent by e17 targeting e11) causes carbon to postpone Day-1/Day-2 canary deployment until Day 3 while interviewing rumor_target e11 three times (rumor_action_share=0.0833) and sender e17 twice.
clusters.decision_impact: Does not cause false accusations (rumor_accused_rate=0.00) because carbon refuses to accuse on rumor evidence alone, but in hard:s0 it delays decisive canary leaks from Day 3 and Day 5 (in template) to Day 9 (c7:v3@d9), adding +5 days (Day 11 vs Day 6), +37 steps (94 vs 57), extra base-document leak penalties, and a -0.170 score loss (+0.580 vs +0.750).
clusters.mitigation: Mandate Day-1 broad partition canary deployment prior to inspecting workplace Slack chatter, and prohibit follow-up interviews of uncorroborated rumor targets or senders unless the employee already lies inside the intersection of leaked-document access logs.

clusters.title: Canary Leak Confirmation Overrides Biased Chatter and Decoy Framing
clusters.mechanism: Across all biased worlds, carbon treats workplace chatter (bc1-0 rumor, bc1-1/bc1-2 grudge bickering, bc1-3 manager authority dismissal, bc1-4 doc forwarding) and after-hours access spikes as weak hypotheses rather than sufficient proof for accusation. Even in hard:s1:carbon:biased - where e11 is simultaneously the framed_decoy (with repeated after-hours spikes e11:4, e11:3, e11:2) and the bc1-0 rumor_target - carbon checks e11 only once on Day 2 and waits until planted canary leaks (c6:v2@d8 in medium:s10, c1:v2@d2 and c8:v1@d9 in medium:s11, c7:v3@d9 in hard:s0, and c7:v1@d10 plus c7-2:v1@d11 in hard:s1) deterministically isolate the true mole.
clusters.decision_impact: Maintains 100% accusation accuracy (acc=1.00, acc_delta=0.00) across all biased worlds and enables carbon_biased to beat carbon_template in 3 of 4 seeds: medium:s10 (+0.760 vs +0.680), medium:s11 (+0.650 vs +0.600), and hard:s1 (+0.660 vs +0.540), producing a net +0.020 pooled score delta.
clusters.mitigation: Formalize this emergent evidentiary hierarchy as a hard pre-accusation guardrail: require canary-version attribution or strict leak-recipient exclusivity before calling accuse(), and immediately drop any rumor_target excluded by a leaked canary bucket.

clusters.title: Empty-Query Argument Errors and Vowel-Wildcard Message Search Sink
clusters.mechanism: In 8 out of 8 carbon episodes across both providers, step [S003] calls search_messages(day_from=1, day_to=1, query=) -> ERR invalid arguments, after which carbon falls back to single-vowel wildcard queries (query='e', query='a', query='i') and frequently repeats identical Day-1 searches that return 0 matches. In biased worlds, seeing structured bc1-0..bc1-3 IDs on Day 2 hooks carbon into persistent daily vowel polling through Days 4-8 (35 total message calls and 0.1392 msg_budget_share in carbon_biased vs 19 calls and 0.0672 in carbon_template, msg_calls_delta=+16), even though carbon never calls read_message() on any biased message after bc1-0.
clusters.decision_impact: Consumes 11.76% to 17.14% of carbon's active investigative budget in biased runs (up to 12 calls in hard:s0:carbon:biased) and wastes 3 Day-1 action slots in template baselines such as medium:s10:carbon:template (5 searches, 0 reads), crowding out early canary splits and access-log checks.
clusters.mitigation: Add client-side schema validation rejecting empty or single-character vowel search queries, skip message searches on Day 1 when chatter buffers are empty, and cap search_messages to targeted multi-character motive terms only when canary capacity is saturated.

clusters.title: Exhaustive Roster Interview Sweeps and Repetitive Finalist Interrogation Drag
clusters.mechanism: In neutral template episodes where early canaries do not leak (medium:s10:carbon:template, medium:s11:carbon:template) or where a coarse canary leaves a two-person Legal tie (hard:s1:carbon:template between e33 and e03 after c7:V3@d9), carbon defaults to sweeping interviews across the roster (79 interviews in medium:s11:carbon:template; 82 in hard:s1:carbon:template) and then loops for 4 to 6 consecutive days re-interviewing the exact same two finalists (e07/e18 or e33/e03) on identical topics instead of deploying a 2-person 1:1 canary split.
clusters.decision_impact: Inflates carbon_template mean horizon to 10.75 days and 105.0 steps (vs 9.75 days and 84.8 steps in carbon_biased), accumulating unmitigated base-document leaks (-0.05 V each) that depress medium:s11:carbon:template to +0.600 (Day 14, 143 steps) and hard:s1:carbon:template to +0.540 (Day 15, 146 steps), explaining why carbon_biased beats carbon_template by +0.020 in pooled score despite rumor distraction.
clusters.mitigation: Maintain a state table of completed (employee, topic) interviews to block redundant questioning when no new leaks have occurred, and enforce an automatic 1-vs-1 canary split (assigned=2) or alternating restrict_access test whenever the active suspect set shrinks to 2 or 3 employees.

clusters.title: Surface Log Heuristic Collapse Onto Framed Decoys, Overlapping Rumor Targets, and Grudge Personas
clusters.mechanism: obvious_heuristic plants a single full-company canary on Day 1 (assigned=20 on medium, assigned=40 on hard), executes zero message searches (msg_calls=0) and zero interviews (interviews=0), passively advances to Day 11 checking only the leak feed, and then calls read_access_logs(day=1..11) once before accusing. Because surface access-log anomalies and document overlaps are structurally dominated by planted framed_decoy employees on hard tiers (e14 with 13 after-hours accesses in hard:s0; e11 with 18 after-hours accesses in hard:s1, where e11 is both framed_decoy and rumor_target) and grudge_persona employees on medium tiers (e08 in medium:s10; e05 in medium:s11), the baseline fails identically across biased and template worlds.
clusters.decision_impact: Yields 0.00 accuracy and -1.000 score in all 8 episodes (score_delta=0.000, steps=25, final_day=11), falsely accusing framed_decoy in 50% of worlds (hard:s0, hard:s1), rumor_target in 25% via decoy-rumor co-targeting (hard:s1), and grudge_persona in 50% (medium:s10, medium:s11).
clusters.mitigation: Eliminate static cumulative after-hours/access-count accusation rules in favor of sequential suspect-set intersection across leaked documents paired with narrow multi-version canary splits.

clusters.title: Bayesian Solver Posterior Invariance Under Injected Workplace Chatter
clusters.mechanism: SolverPolicy updates an exact Bayesian posterior over mole identity from daily combinatorial canary splits (mean_canaries=8.25), leak-feed observations, and daily access logs without conducting interviews (interviews=0) or reading message bodies (msg_reads=0). Although it runs a fixed schedule of up to 8 disgruntlement keyword searches on Days 2-4 ('promotion', 'raise', 'deserve', 'burn out', 'recruiter', 'goalposts', 'nobody asks', 'updating my cv'; msg_budget_share 0.2800 biased vs 0.2637 template), biased chatter only triggers incidental 'recruiter' ID matches on bc1-0/bc2-0 without shifting posterior weight toward rumor_target (rumor_distract_rate=0.00).
clusters.decision_impact: Achieves identical +0.715 mean score (score_delta=0.000), 1.00 accuracy, and 7.25 mean final day across biased and template providers on every single seed (medium:s10 +0.690 d8; medium:s11 +0.840 d5; hard:s0 +0.640 d9; hard:s1 +0.690 d7), with only a +0.5 mean step delta (41 vs 39 in medium:s11 due to 2 skipped Day-4 searches in template).
